chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the male slave: how many women are permissible for him? He said: 'Only two are permissible for him, and he may take concubines as he wishes, if his master permits him.'

key_terms.يَتَسَرَّى: He takes concubines / takes to his bed

ai.seo_question: How many wives and concubines is a male slave permitted to have according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the marital status of a male slave (mamluk), permitting him up to two wives and unlimited concubines (sariyyah) contingent upon his master's consent. This ruling highlights the distinct legal capacity of slaves in Shia jurisprudence, where the master's authority over the slave's personal life intersects with the slave's right to establish a household, reflecting the socio-economic realities of the time.
